sentences.text: The Honourable Smt. Justice K. Sujana

Criminal Petition No.8346 of 2023
Order:

This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short 'Cr.P.C.') by the petitioners/accused, seeking to quash the proceedings against him in Crime No.81 of 2023 of PS Bollarum, on the file XXII Additinal Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, at Secunderabad.
2. Though notice is served, there is no representation for respondent No.2.

3. Heard Sri Nageshwar Rao Pujari, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri S.Ganesh, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor for respondent No.1 - State.
4.

The de-facto complainant/respondent No.2 filed a written complaint before the police on 21.08.2023 stating that she is working in Sri Garitha Finance Company, Alwal as third party BPO employee and in March, 2021 and while working from home as usually, she called to SKS,J customers' list for loan process.
Meanwhile, she called the petitioner herein and they both had a general talk other than loan process and thereafter the petitioner enquired about her whereabouts.
Since then both started talking to each other regularly over calls.
After six (06) months, they both met at Patny Circle and went to Chilkur Balaji Temple on petitioner's two-wheeler.
Later, the petitioner promised respondent No.2 for marriage and after two (02) months, he took her to his residence at Vanasthalipuram and they both physically committed with mutual consent.
Later on many times, the petitioner took respondent No.2 to his house and they both had physical relationship.

They also went to 'Stay-in Hotel' at Flat No.155B, Inorbit Mall Road, Kavuri Hills,
Phase 2 Road, Near D Mart, Doctor's Colony, Madhapur few times.
Respondent No.2 asked the petitioner about marriage and he always said he will come and talk to her parents, but now the petitioner is cheating and refusing to marry her.
Therefore, she SKS,J requested to take necessary action against the petitioner herein.

5. Basing on the aforesaid complaint, respondent No.1 registered a case against the petitioner vide Crime No.81 of 2023 for the offences under Sections 376(2)(n), 417 and 420 of I.P.C.
6.
The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that respondent No.2 is misusing the law and the same can be garnered by the statements of the witnesses and the victim, made before the Magistrate.
Hence, continuation of the impugned proceedings against the petitioner is gross abuse of process of law.

Learned counsel further submits that the Hon'ble Apex Court in a catena of judgment drew distinction between mere breach of promise and not fulfilling promise in case where the accusation is that of rape under the misconception of marriage.

It is contended that the investigating agency has done table investigation and has completely disregarded the distinction Kovelampati Karthik, vs The State Of Telangana on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85674835/
1 between mere breach of promise and a lawful promise.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the SKS,J petitioner further contends that the law is settled with regard to the consent of a woman with respect to Section 375 of I.P.C., it must involve an active and reasoned deliberation to the proposed act to establish whether the consent was vitiated by a misconception of a fact arising out of a promise to marriage.

To establish the same, two propositions must be established:- (1) the promise of marriage must have been a false promise, given in bad faith and with no intention of being adhered to at the time it was given; and (2) the false promise must be of immediate relevance and it should bear direct nexus with the woman's decision to engage in the sexual act.
The said ingredients are completely absent from in the present case.

7. Learned counsel for the petitioner contends that, even if the contents of the complaint are to be accepted as gospel truth, they would not attract any ingredients to constitute offences under Sections 376(2)(n), 417 and 420 of I.P.C.
Further, the complaint itself shows that there is no promise of marriage made by the petitioner SKS,J before the consent for consensual cohabitation.
Therefore, prayed this Court to quash the proceedings in Crime No.81 of 2023 of PS Bollarum, on the file XXII Additinal Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, at Secunderabad.

entities.text: XXII Additinal Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, at Secunderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 8. Per contra, the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor would submit that the offences alleged against the petitioner are heinous and they require trial as such, prayed this Court to dismiss the present petition.

9. From the perusal of the record, it is disclosed that Crime No.81 of 2023 is registered against the petitioner for the alleged offences punishable Sections 376(2)(n), 417 and 420 of I.P.C., basing on the complaint filed by respondent No.2.
Respondent No.2, in her complaint alleged that the petitioner herein had engaged in sexual intercourse with her under the guise of marriage.

Admittedly, petitioner and respondent No.2 got acquainted when respondent No.2 called the petitioner for the loan process and according to respondent No.2 they had general talk with each other over the phone and SKS,J they also met several times at the house of petitioner.

Further, the physical relation between the petitioner and respondent No.2 was with her consent and the parties had cohabitation multiple times without any resistance or complaint from respondent No.2.
10.

Section 375 of I.P.C., in Explanation-2 says "consent means an unequivocal voluntary agreement when the woman by words, gestures or any form of verbal or non-verbal communication,
communicates willingness to participate in the specific sexual act".

Section 90 of I.P.C. enumerates:-
"a consent is not such a consent as it intended by any section of this Code, if the consent is given by a person under fear of injury, or under a misconception of fact, and if the person doing the act knows,
or has reason to believe, that the consent was given in consequence of such fear or misconception.".

11. The primary contention of respondent No.2 is that the petitioner herein engaged in sexual relationship with her under the false promise of marriage, therefore, her consent was under misconception of fact.

2 12.

sentences.text: In the present case, the 'misconception of fact' alleged by respondent No.2 is that the petitioner had promised to marry her.

Specifically in the context of a promise to marry, there must be a distinction between a false promise given on the understanding by the maker that it will be broken,
and the breach of a promise which is made in good faith but subsequently not fulfilled.

13. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pramod Surabhan Pawar Vs. State of Maharashtra and Another 1, held as under :
"18.

entities.text: Pramod Surabhan Pawar Vs. State of Maharashtra and Another 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: To summarize the legal position that emerges from the above cases, the "consent" of a woman with respect to Section 375 must involve an active and reasoned deliberation towards the proposed act.

To establish whether the "consent"
was vitiated by a "misconception of fact" arising out of a promise to marry, two propositions must be established.
The promise of marriage must have been a false promise, given in bad faith and with no intention of being adhered to at the time it was given.

The false promise itself must be of immediate relevance, or bear a direct nexus to the woman's decision to engage in the sexual act."
14.

Having regard to the rival submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and the aforesaid decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, this Court is 1 (2019) 9 Supreme Court Cases 608 SKS,J of the considered opinion that in the instant case the allegations raised by respondent No.2 in her complaint, prima facie, shows that the petitioner herein promised respondent No.2 that he would marry her and under the guise of said promise respondent No.2 indulged in physical relationship with the petitioner.

15. As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pramod Surabhan Pawar's case (1 supra),
the promise of marriage must have been a false promise given in bad faith and with no intention of being adhered to at the time it was given.
The averments in the complaint shows that the petitioner made a promise of marriage to respondent No.2, as such she consented for sexual intercourse and later the petitioner refused to marry.
Whether the promise made by the petitioner is false or a promise given in bad faith cannot be decided without a full fledged trial.
Therefore, there are no merits in the petitioner and the same is liable to be dismissed.
SKS,J 16.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, this criminal petition is dismissed as devoid of merits.
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, in this Criminal Petition shall stand closed.
_ _ JUSTICE K. SUJANA March 15, 2024.
